edits.old: And the record names the archive location that proves where the rows went
edits.new:
And the record names the archive location that proves where the rows went

  Scenario: AC10 A decision code outside LOV-DECISION is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns LOV-DECISION with the archive and purge decision codes in force
    When rwb-document offers the record of an archive action whose decision code is not in LOV-DECISION in force
    Then the ledger refuses the record with MSG-P7-009
    And no decision_log_entry row is written and no chain_seq is consumed
    And the decision code and final call are read from the reference-data client in the version in force, not written in code

  Scenario: AC11 An unauthenticated read of the decision log is answered 401 (new, D-RCV-60)
    When a caller without a credential reads GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log or GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}
    Then the answer is 401 for each operation
    And no DecisionLogPage and no entry is returned

  Scenario: AC12 A retried or timed-out activity writes one record (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document activity that writes the record of an archive action times out before the decision-record library answers
    When the activity is retried with the same event ID and idempotency key
    Then one decision_log_entry row exists for the action and no second chain_seq is consumed
    And an activity that timed out before the append writes no entry, consumes no chain_seq and commits no archive or delete
